description: Student passionate about AI, space, and research.
summary:
ASTAR (Autonomous Surface Traversal & Astronaut Routing) is an interactive 3D Martian EVA mission planner built on real NASA MRO CTX elevation and orbital imagery of Jezero Crater.

Addressing the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, ASTAR moves beyond naive shortest-path routing, which often leads astronauts and rovers across lethal crater scarps, loose aeolian sand traps, and dense boulder fields. Using classical computer vision combined with an 8-connected weighted A* planner, ASTAR computes routes that enforce slope limits, minimize hazard exposure, and compare safe detours directly against unconstrained shortest baselines. It also models simulated PLSS oxygen and battery consumption to verify round-trip feasibility, while matching orbital terrain classes to real NASA Perseverance Mastcam-Z imagery via OpenCLIP.

As human and robotic Mars exploration expands, resource-aware, hazard-avoiding navigation is critical for crew survival and emergency return planning.
details:
ASTAR (Autonomous Surface Traversal & Astronaut Routing) is an interactive 3D EVA mission-control and path-planning web application for Jezero Crater, Mars. Using real NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) CTX orbital elevation and imagery, ASTAR renders an interactive Three.js 3D terrain mesh with three switchable layers: Orbital, Slope Risk (<8°, 8°–15°, >15°), and Surface Hazard.

A classical computer vision pipeline (SciPy / NumPy) detects boulder roughness from local 9×9 orbital variance and loose sand traps from low-albedo smooth regolith, producing a non-linear hazard cost grid. An 8-connected weighted A* planner computes optimal routes under hard slope limits, overlays a Cyan (Safe A*) vs. Orange (Unconstrained Shortest) comparison, supports one-click Abort to Hab emergency return routing, and estimates EVA duration, climb, O2 (800 g tank), battery (1200 Wh), and round-trip safety (<45% one-way reserve threshold). In Orbit or First-Person traversal modes, ASTAR matches orbital terrain conditions to NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Mastcam-Z photos and runs zero-shot OpenCLIP (ViT-B-32) terrain classification for live ground-level reconnaissance.

Benefits & intended impact: Straight-line paths on Mars often cross lethal crater walls or soft sand traps that risk astronaut falls, rover immobilization, or life-support exhaustion. ASTAR bridges orbital hazard mapping, resource-aware routing, and ground-level visual verification into one intuitive mission-planning tool for safer EVA operations.

Tools, languages & software:

Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, OpenCLIP (ViT-B-32), unittest

Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript, Three.js (OrbitControls), HTML5/CSS3

Data & Design: NASA MRO CTX Jezero Crater DEM & Mosaic, NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Raw Images, Canva

Creativity & factors considered:

Honest data boundaries: Clearly separates real NASA orbital/rover datasets from simulated PLSS life-support estimates and classical CV hazard masks.

Dual-route explainability: Visually proves why A* detours around hazards compared to an unconstrained shortest-path baseline.

Safety-first constraints: Hard slope cutoffs, round-trip O2/battery reserve checks (45% one-way cap), and emergency Abort to Hab routing.
